_comment: Canonical documentation-media shot manifest. Every entry is a real render of a real corpus file, captured by tools/screenshots/capture.mjs on the shared mid-grey documentation presentation (lib/presentation.mjs). Regenerate all: `node capture.mjs`. Subset: `node capture.mjs <name> ...`. Keep captions/alt in sync with what the image shows (USER_FACING_DOCS_STYLE §8).
colorPalettes: resolved from lib/presentation.mjs PAL by mode

shots.name: viewer-benchy-tubes
shots.caption: 3DBenchy rendered as extrusion tubes, colored by feature role.
shots.alt: 3DBenchy rendered as extrusion tubes with per-feature coloring — perimeters, infill, and skirt in distinct colors — on a neutral grey build plate

shots.name: layer-clip-benchy
shots.caption: Layer-range clipping: the model cut to a mid-height band, exposing perimeters and infill.
shots.alt: 3DBenchy clipped to a mid-height layer range, cutting through the cabin to expose perimeters and infill

shots.name: color-speed-calicat
shots.caption: Color by feedrate: blue at slow moves ramping to red at fast moves.
shots.alt: The calicat model colored by feedrate, from blue at slow moves to red at fast moves

shots.name: color-layerheight
shots.caption: Color by layer height: thin layers blue, thick layers red — variable-layer regions at a glance.
shots.alt: A variable-layer-height test print colored from blue for thin layers to red for thick layers

shots.name: cnc-cut-vs-rapid
shots.caption: An Easel CNC carve colored by move kind: cut moves pink, rapid moves blue.
shots.alt: An Easel CNC carve toolpath colored by move kind: cut moves in pink, rapid moves in blue

shots.name: progress-known
shots.caption: Live progress from byte-exact telemetry: a precise cut and an exact position marker.
shots.alt: Live-progress overlay with a byte-exact position: completed toolpath in full color, remaining path as a translucent ghost, and an orange marker at the exact print position

shots.name: progress-approximated
shots.caption: Live progress from a coarse signal: an emphasis band spanning the current layer, not a false-precise dot.
shots.alt: Live-progress overlay from a coarse signal: an emphasis band spanning the current layer instead of a single false-precise marker

shots.name: camera-top
shots.caption: Top preset (orthographic).
shots.alt: 3DBenchy from directly above, orthographic camera — the hull outline

shots.name: camera-front
shots.caption: Front preset (orthographic).
shots.alt: 3DBenchy from the front, orthographic camera — the boat's side profile

shots.name: camera-iso
shots.caption: Iso preset (perspective).
shots.alt: 3DBenchy from an isometric angle, perspective camera

shots.name: retraction-markers
shots.caption: Retraction and de-retraction markers pinned on the toolpath.
shots.alt: Calicat lower layers with retraction and de-retraction markers as orange and cyan pins on the toolpath

shots.name: app-control-panel
shots.caption: The demo application: control panel beside a fully rendered 3DBenchy.
shots.alt: The demo application: a control panel — corpus picker, layer and time scrub, an honest print-time estimate, display toggles — beside a fully rendered 3DBenchy with feature coloring

shots.name: canvas-2d-fallback
shots.caption: The Canvas 2D fallback: a flat layer view with no WebGL and no Three.js.
shots.alt: A single print layer drawn by the Canvas 2D renderer: perimeter walls and cross-hatch infill, no WebGL

shots.name: model-render-stl-3mf
shots.caption: Presentation stills from renderModelStill: a neutral STL (materials: unavailable) beside a colored 3MF (materials: known).
shots.alt: Two presentation thumbnails from renderModelStill: left, a neutral gray part from an STL labeled materials unavailable; right, a colored tower from a 3MF labeled materials known

shots.name: parametric-bolt-circle
shots.caption: An RS274NGC parametric program: a bolt circle and frame COMPUTED from parameters (a while-loop + subroutine + degree trig), rendered as the real toolpath.
shots.alt: A CNC toolpath of eight drilled holes on a circle plus a centre hole and a square frame, all computed by a parametric program, cut moves in pink and rapid moves in blue

shots.name: bed-circular
shots.caption: A circular (delta-style) build bed: the outline and grid follow the round shape, not a rectangle.
shots.alt: A print rendered on a round, delta-style build plate — the bed outline and grid are circular, with the model centered on it

shots.name: bed-polygon
shots.caption: A polygonal build bed: an arbitrary hexagonal bed outline with the grid clipped to the shape.
shots.alt: A print rendered on a hexagonal build plate — the bed outline is a six-sided polygon with the grid clipped to it

shots.name: render-tubes
shots.caption: Tube geometry: lit 3D extrusion cross-sections.
shots.alt: The calicat rendered as lit 3D extrusion tubes

shots.name: render-lines
shots.caption: Line geometry: flat one-pixel paths — lighter, for very large files or low-GPU devices.
shots.alt: The calicat rendered as flat single-pixel toolpath lines

shots.name: scrub-sweep
shots.caption: Segment scrub: stepping the draw-range through the toolpath traces the exact print order — the animation IS the feature.
shots.alt: Animation of 3DBenchy drawing itself as the segment scrub sweeps from the first move to the last

shots.name: layer-buildup
shots.caption: Layer-range sweep: raising the top layer builds the model up bottom to top — the progressive reveal, shown as motion.
shots.alt: Animation of 3DBenchy building up layer by layer from the base to the top as the layer range grows
